Negative‑sampling‑enhanced contrastive graph learning has been applied to academic reviewer recommendation, demonstrating the versatility of GCL across domains [S2:a280deb68d656acbdf28adb82ccfdddac1d8886f]. Counterfactual intervention techniques have been integrated with graph contrastive learning to address implicit‑feedback biases in recommendation [S2:ade0b7f79e5cdeee4f6d4f23e4f97f382b786d34]. Multi‑behavior recommendation scenarios benefit from graph contrastive learning that jointly models diverse interaction types [S2:4e1e1cc795d3ec3ff51c9b28bc1d9e6c7f09662f].

Simplified graph contrastive learning frameworks directly optimize alignment and uniformity objectives to streamline training for recommendation tasks [S2:2453ed89166b6a6f4765bd07cfe83fcac041ac37]. Simultaneous local and global contrastive objectives have been proposed to capture hierarchical graph structures in recommender models [S2:dd7944eed93a9636f4cbce7ac68125f2bbdabd92]. Structure‑augmentation combined with attribute‑aware contrastive learning mitigates weak‑information scenarios by enriching graph views [S2:b6e8b6d09e90c728885693fd9f32d6a6593306a5]. Robust graph contrastive learning approaches address data sparsity and noise, enhancing recommendation reliability under real‑world conditions [S2:90eed4e1cc8f13a8ece64328cd8219e06c13d0e9].
